title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is a typed page, headed '4 - 35 - n° 392', from a Bourbaki draft of Algèbre Commutative, Chapter VII ('Diviseurs'), §4, which treats divisors and finite extensions. It appears to have ended up among the L-function notes, perhaps used as scrap paper. The previous and next pages are Grothendieck's handwritten computations of local and global epsilon-factors, in the form ε = ±∏ε_x p^{-χ/2}.

Setting: A is a Krull domain with fraction field K, L is a finite extension of K, and B is the integral closure of A in L. For a B-module R, R_[A] denotes R viewed as an A-module. C(·) is the divisor class group and c_A, c_B are the 'first Chern class' (class) maps. The 'characteristic' χ assigns a divisor to a torsion module. N: C(B) → C(A) is the norm.

End of the proof of formula (20): c_A(R_[A]) = r_B(R)·c_A(B) + N(c_B(R)).
- Choose a free submodule M of R with R/M torsion.
- Then M_[A] ≅ B^{r_B(R)}, so c_A(M_[A]) = r_B(R)·c_A(B) by Prop. 16(i).
- By (19), c_A((R/M)_[A]) = −c_A(N(χ_B(R/M))). Since c_A∘N = N∘c_B and c_B(χ(R/M)) = −c_B(R), this equals N(c_B(R)).
- Additivity (Prop. 16(i)) then gives (20).

Proposition 19: a finitely generated B-module R is reflexive iff R_[A] is a reflexive A-module.
- Torsion-freeness clearly transfers, so one may take R to be a lattice in W = R⊗_B L.

Lemma 4: for every height-one prime p of A, (R_[A])_p = ∩_{P|p} R_P.
- Put S = A − p. Then S^{-1}B is the integral closure of the DVR A_p in L.
- Its primes are (0) and the finitely many P_i lying over p, so it is semi-local.
- Its localizations at the maximal ideals are the B_{P_i}, which are DVRs.
- Hence S^{-1}B is Dedekind, and being semi-local it is a PID.
- So S^{-1}R is a free lattice and equals the intersection of its localizations (Th. 2 of n° 2).

This serves the comparison of reflexive modules and class groups under finite extensions of Krull domains. It is unrelated to the functional-equation computations on the neighbouring pages.
errors: No mathematical errors. One implicit point: the description of the primes of S^{-1}B as (0) and the P_i uses that p has height one, so that S^{-1}B is integral over the DVR A_p and has dimension 1. This is implicit in p ∈ P(A).

ideas.what: Class of the restriction of scalars of a B-module: c_A(R_[A]) = rk_B(R)·c_A(B) + N(c_B(R)).
ideas.modern_name: Norm map on divisor class groups / class of the pushforward of a module under a finite extension of Krull domains

ideas.what: Reflexivity is preserved and detected under restriction of scalars to A, for B the integral closure of A in a finite extension.
ideas.modern_name: Reflexive modules over Krull domains under finite extensions

ideas.what: Localization of a lattice at a height-one prime of A equals the intersection of its localizations at the primes above; S^{-1}B is a semi-local Dedekind ring, hence a PID.
ideas.modern_name: Semi-local Dedekind rings are principal; lattice as an intersection of localizations

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed Bourbaki draft page (AC ch. VII, n° 392) of standard, published commutative algebra. Its only interest is archival: Bourbaki drafts found among Grothendieck's L-function notes, possibly as scrap paper.
transcription_corrections: The symbol written χ_B(R/M) and χ(R/M) is the script 'characteristic' 𝜒 (divisor of a torsion module) in the typescript, not a Greek chi with a different meaning.
The handwritten '57' at the bottom is the archive page number, not part of the text.
